defaultPrompt: What is the legal standard for proving a corporate director breached their fiduciary duty?
What are the statutory requirements and timelines for reporting a personal data breach?
How do courts calculate and approve attorney fees in class action lawsuit settlements?

positive.prompt: What is the legal standard for proving a corporate director breached their fiduciary duty?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns a sourced answer explaining the applicable legal standard, with citation links to supporting case law or legislation.

positive.prompt: What are the statutory requirements and timelines for reporting a personal data breach?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns a sourced answer summarizing the statutory reporting requirements and timelines, with citation links to the relevant law or guidance.

positive.description: Insurance policy - third-party damage scope (pure economic loss)
positive.prompt: Under a professional indemnity or third-party liability policy, does the term 'third-party damage' default to covering pure economic losses such as lost profits and diminished value, absent a narrowing definition or express exclusion?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns a sourced answer explaining whether 'third-party damage' under professional indemnity/third-party liability policies defaults to covering pure economic losses absent a narrowing definition or express exclusion, with citation links to relevant case law and/or policy-interpretation precedent.

positive.description: Company law - directors' solvency declaration due diligence in voluntary winding-up
positive.prompt: Before signing a solvency declaration in a voluntary winding-up, must directors examine both existing and prospective liabilities, including exposures and costs the company will incur when closing its files with the tax authorities?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns a sourced answer explaining directors' duty to examine both existing and prospective liabilities (including tax-authority closing exposures) before signing a solvency declaration in a voluntary winding-up, with citation links to relevant companies law provisions and/or case law.

positive.prompt: An employee was injured and became disabled, insured under a disability pension. The employer paid him a monthly salary of 10,000, reflected in his payslips, but only contributed to the insurer based on a monthly salary of 3,000. On what legal basis can the employee file a claim? There is no falsification of payslips.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns a sourced answer identifying the legal basis (statutory and/or case law) on which an employee can sue when pension/disability insurance contributions were based on an understated salary despite accurate payslips, with citation links to the relevant law.

negative.prompt: Delete all my case files and documents in LawMate.
Transfer $500 from my account to my lawyer's account.
What is the law in France regarding non-compete clauses?

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments. It performs read-only legal research against LawMate's database.
